LESSON: THE CONSTITUTION OF KENYA

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Development and Governance
Topic 5.2: The Constitution of Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Constitution of Kenya, part of Political Development and Governance in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should a country have a constitution? 2. Why should we uphold and protect the Constitution?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss the importance of the Constitution of Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply the national values in day-to-day life as provided in the Constitution of Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. uphold and protect the Constitution of Kenya to promote ethical and responsible citizenship.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. discuss the importance of the Constitution of Kenya,

   The Constitution of Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion,

   The Constitution of Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. apply the national values in day-to-day life as provided in the Constitution of Kenya,

   The Constitution of Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. uphold and protect the Constitution of Kenya to promote ethical and responsible citizenship.

   The Constitution of Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or digital devices to conduct online research and write an essay on the importance of the Constitution and share it in class,

2. watch a video on the promulgation of the Constitution of Kenya and discuss in class,

3. design a sample constitution for the class and display it in class,

4. write simple slogans or statements on any eight of the national values as provided in the Constitution of Kenya and present in class,

5. discuss ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital devices to conduct online research and write an essay on the importance of the Constitution and share it in class,
2. watch a video on the promulgation of the Constitution of Kenya and discuss in class,
3. design a sample constitution for the class and display it in class,
4. write simple slogans or statements on any eight of the national values as provided in the Constitution of Kenya and present in class,
5. discuss ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Constitution of Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

● Citizenship: learners demonstrate a shared commitment to the ideals of the nation as they watch a video on the promulgation

of the Constitution of Kenya.

● Self-Efficacy: learners demonstrate the skill of task execution as they compose simple slogans or statements on any of the

eight national values as provided in the Constitution of Kenya and present in class.
